title: Registry Binding File
description: One bindings/<platform>/<integration>.json artifact. Compiler-facing. Kept out of the capability file because the n8n bindings are machine-generated on every regeneration while the Make and Zapier bindings are hand-curated, and putting a generator's output and human curation in one file guarantees eventual clobbering. Adding a platform then adds a directory and touches no existing file.

platform.description: The target key. Must match the directory this file sits in.

bindings.description: Keyed by capability ID, the join key to the capability file. A null value means this platform genuinely cannot do this and degrades to http.request.send with a warning. An absent key means not yet mapped, which is a registry gap. The compiler treats them differently, so the format has to be able to say both.

parameterValue.description: Any JSON literal. A platform's fixed parameter values are whatever that platform accepts.

staticParameters.description: Platform params with fixed values and no FFIR equivalent. n8n's Slack node needs resource: message and operation: post to mean send a message; those live here rather than polluting FFIR with platform vocabulary.

additionalProperties.description: The platform path. Dots mean nesting, so otherOptions.thread_ts builds a nested object.

parameterMap.description: Build validation rule 4: every key must name a parameter the capability declares.

transformMap.description: Names a function in the target's closed, unit-tested transform table. Arbitrary transform code in registry data would make the registry executable, and generated registry data must never be executable.

type_version.description: Pinned. Bumping it is a deliberate act.

binding.description: A binding is shaped by its platform. n8n names a node type and a pinned version, Make names a module, Zapier names an app and an action. Only n8n is bound in the MVP; the other two are declared because the format has to prove it can carry them before the claim that adding a platform is cheap means anything.
